drhp.business: Arabian Petroleum manufactures a wide range of lubricants including specialty oils, coolants, greases and process oils for Industrial and Automotive applications, organised into two product divisions — Automotive Lubricants (Arzol) and Industrial Lubricants. It serves private-sector customers across pharmaceutical, FMCG, chemicals, steel, rubber and tyre, power, civil engineering, electrical appliances, textile, telecommunication and automobile industries, alongside central/state government and defence customers, and exports to more than 30 countries.

risks.note: Volatility in the prices of base oils, additives, packaging materials and other raw materials continues to influence margins across the lubricant value chain.
FX movements may impact the cost of imported raw materials and components.
Increasing competition from domestic and international lubricant manufacturers continues to place pressure on pricing, product innovation and customer service.

Growth in electric vehicles is gradually changing the long-term demand profile for conventional automotive engine oils, though conventional lubricants remain important for the existing vehicle parc and hybrid applications.

International crude oil prices remain subject to volatility from geopolitical developments, supply/demand changes and disruptions in major energy-producing regions, directly affecting the cost of petroleum-based raw materials.

BS-VI emission standards and evolving vehicle technologies are increasing the requirement for technically advanced lubricants, and customers increasingly demand environmentally responsible, energy-efficient and technically superior solutions.

The Board states a risk-management mechanism covers risk mapping, trend analysis, risk exposure, potential impact and mitigation, with an exercise ongoing to identify, evaluate, manage and monitor both business and non-business risks.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Volatility in the prices of base oils, additives, packaging materials and other raw materials continues to influence margins across the lubricant value chain.
- FX movements may impact the cost of imported raw materials and components.
- Increasing competition from domestic and international lubricant manufacturers continues to place pressure on pricing, product innovation and customer service.
- Growth in electric vehicles is gradually changing the long-term demand profile for conventional automotive engine oils, though conventional lubricants remain important for the existing vehicle parc and hybrid applications.
- International crude oil prices remain subject to volatility from geopolitical developments, supply/demand changes and disruptions in major energy-producing regions, directly affecting the cost of petroleum-based raw materials.
- BS-VI emission standards and evolving vehicle technologies are increasing the requirement for technically advanced lubricants, and customers increasingly demand environmentally responsible, energy-efficient and technically superior solutions.
- The Board states a risk-management mechanism covers risk mapping, trend analysis, risk exposure, potential impact and mitigation, with an exercise ongoing to identify, evaluate, manage and monitor both business and non-business risks.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Convert expanded manufacturing capacity into profitable volume.
- Keep shifting product mix towards specialty, food-grade and defence-grade products where differentiation is strongest.
- Deepen backward integration so more value is created in-house, lowering input costs.
- Broaden reach in export markets and across the two subsidiaries (Arzol Petroleum Trading FZE and Lavisa Technologies).
- Keep defence, aerospace and institutional supply at the core of the business.
- Strengthen the Industrial and Automotive lubricants product portfolio to consolidate market position and broaden offering …
